narr: Surface low pressure was drifting across the Quad State on the 14th. Showers and thunderstorms developed in the afternoon to evening with Southwest Indiana seeing storms drift slowly northeastward. CAPE values around 1000 J/kg dropped off after sunset. Lapse rates were around 6.5 C/km, and shear was limited to around 25 kts. Despite also producing cold air funnels, one storm produced a brief EF-1 tornado on the northeast side of Newburgh. Torrential rainfall of 3-5.5 inches fell in Warrick County, producing widespread flash flooding for the late afternoon and evening hours.
ev: Widespread flooding occurred in Warrick County north of Newburgh. Fire officials reported flash flooding at Lincoln and Epworth Rd near Deaconess Gateway. Fire officials also reported that Oak Grove Rd was flooded due to drainage ditches out of their banks east of Anderson Rd and Coal Mine Rd flooded near Telephone Rd with moving water. News media reported roadway flooding near Grimm Rd and Willow Pond Rd. Waters rose into neighborhoods, businesses, and farmland along SR 66. 3-5 inches of rainfall fell on the 14th with most of the rain occurring in the late afternoon hours. A measuring site at Deaconess Gateway reported over 5.5 inches of rain for the day as of 1700CST. CoCoRaHS sites in Newburgh reported 2.75-3.65 inches of rain just south of the hardest hit locations.
